Everything we offer / Heritage walk

The Qutb complex

A guided heritage walk through a World Heritage Site, read from its inscriptions and masonry

On request

Arranged for your group. Send your preferred dates, group size and location. We adapt the length, level and language, and prepare a quotation. The suggested group size is a guide, not a requirement.

Request on WhatsApp Request by email

No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The Qutb Minar stands beside a mosque built with reused temple pillars, an iron pillar of the Gupta period and the Alai Darwaza of 1311. The walk uses the inscriptions and the joints in the masonry to trace how the complex grew under successive rulers.

The date, start time, pace and language are arranged to suit your group.

What it covers

  • The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and its reused temple pillars
  • The Iron Pillar and its Gupta-period Sanskrit inscription
  • The Qutb Minar storey by storey, and who built which
  • The Alai Darwaza, Iltutmish's tomb and the unfinished Alai Minar

How the time is spent

  1. Entrance orientation 25 min

    Explain Sultanate building history and UNESCO ensemble.

    You: identify historical phases

  2. Quwwat-ul-Islam and iron pillar 40 min

    Examine reused materials and inscription evidence without oversimplifying.

    You: record two observations

  3. Qutb Minar viewpoints 40 min

    Read tower sections, geometry and calligraphy.

    You: draw profile

  4. Alai Darwaza/Alai Minar 25 min

    Discuss patronage and unfinished schemes.

    You: compare planned versus surviving structures

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Identify and interpret key features of Qutb Complex using material evidence and a site map.
  • Understand early Sultanate architecture, construction and inscriptions.
  • Distinguish directly visible fabric from reconstructed or debated historical claims.

You take away

Your annotated field card, sketches and notes.

Where
Mehrauli, Delhi
For
Schools, colleges, companies and the public
Length
2 to 3 hours
When
Any day you choose. Early morning is best in the warmer months.
Led by
An archaeologist
Language
English, Hindi or both. Other languages on request, through our partners.
Group size
About 10 is suggested. Smaller and larger groups are welcome.
Meeting point
Agreed with you. A map location is shared once the date is confirmed.
What to bring
Comfortable shoes, water and a hat. The ground is uneven in places.
Entry fees
Monument entry fees, where charged, are not included.

Quoted for your group
